slides.templateDescription: Highlight important details in an image

waypoints.caption: ### Food Standards require that **potentially hazardous foods** are kept **below 5°C**
## The food safety **danger zone** exists between these two limits. Bacteria will start forming on food kept in the temperature danger zone.
## The requirement for **cooked meat** is that it is either **hot or cold**.
## To comply with the national food safety standards, **hot meat** must be stored and/or served at **60°C or higher**
## and **cold meat** must be served and/or stored at **5°C or lower**.

images.caption: To defrost food like meat protein. It should be placed in a container and refrigerator for up to 7 days to defrost.
## Defrosting in the **refrigerator** is our **standard and safest** as it doesn't expose food to danger zone temperatures (between 5°C to 60°C).
## The only drawback to this method is that it takes a long time, **at least 24 hours for every 2.5kg**.
## Defrosting under **cold running water** is to be done only in **emergencies **and is the **least preferred **method as it exposes the food to temperatures within the danger zone.
## Defrosting under water **cannot exceed a maximum of 2 hours**.
## Two learn the step-by-step procedure of defrosting, please take a look at the document in the briefcase titled '**Defrosting Procedure**'.

content.content: ## Each state has its own designated **Food Safety Program and Records**. All stores must complete and keep all records safely for a **minimum of 2 years**.
## This will assist you and others in monitoring your store's **food safety practices and hygiene**.

The Food Safety Programs and Records of all states are stored under:

  1. Team Member Hub

  2. Training Home

  3. Store Documents & Guides

  4. Food Safety & Emergency Procedure
